dims.label: Child care
dims.question: Can families find licensed, rated child care near home?
dims.agencies: Georgia Department of Early Care and Learning (licensing, Quality Rated, the Childcare and Parent Services subsidy program and Georgia's Pre-K Program); U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families (Child Care and Development Fund, Head Start).
dims.programs: Childcare and Parent Services (CAPS) subsidies, Quality Rated, Georgia's Pre-K Program, Head Start and Early Head Start.

dims.label: Education
dims.question: Are students learning, showing up and finishing school?
dims.agencies: Local school districts and charter schools; Georgia Department of Education; Governor's Office of Student Achievement; U.S. Department of Education (Title I, special education).
dims.programs: Quality Basic Education state funding, Title I, IDEA special education, school meals.

dims.label: Economic security
dims.question: Do households have enough income to cover basic needs?
dims.agencies: Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services (SNAP, TANF cash aid); USDA Food and Nutrition Service (SNAP); Social Security Administration (SSI); Internal Revenue Service (Earned Income Tax Credit).
dims.programs: SNAP, TANF, SSI, Earned Income Tax Credit, WIC, school meals, home energy assistance.

dims.label: Jobs and workforce
dims.question: Can working-age residents find work that pays?
dims.agencies: Georgia Department of Labor (unemployment insurance, career centers); local workforce development boards; Technical College System of Georgia; U.S. Department of Labor.
dims.programs: Unemployment insurance, Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act training, apprenticeships, technical college programs.

dims.label: Housing
dims.question: Is housing affordable, stable and in decent shape?
dims.agencies: Local public housing authorities (vouchers, public housing); Georgia Department of Community Affairs (Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, vouchers where there is no local authority, Community Development Block Grants and HOME for smaller communities); U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
dims.programs: Housing Choice Vouchers, public housing, project-based rental assistance, Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, HOME, CDBG.

dims.label: Physical health
dims.question: Are residents healthy, covered and able to see a doctor?
dims.agencies: Georgia Department of Community Health (Medicaid, PeachCare for Kids); Georgia Department of Public Health and county health departments; federally funded community health centers (HRSA).
dims.programs: Medicaid, PeachCare for Kids, Georgia Pathways to Coverage, Medicare, community health centers, local public health programs.

dims.label: Mental health
dims.question: Are residents in distress, and can they get treatment?
dims.agencies: Georgia Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities and community service boards; Georgia Department of Community Health (Medicaid); 988 crisis line.
dims.programs: Medicaid behavioral health, community service board services, federal opioid response and settlement funds, crisis services.

dims.label: Public safety
dims.question: Are residents safe from crime and crashes?
dims.agencies: City police, county sheriffs and the courts; Georgia Department of Public Safety (Georgia State Patrol); Governor's Office of Highway Safety; Criminal Justice Coordinating Council; Georgia Attorney General.
dims.programs: Local police and fire budgets, victim services, highway safety grants, violence prevention grants.

dims.label: Social well-being
dims.question: Are residents connected to each other and to community resources?
dims.agencies: Local and regional library systems (with state support through Georgia Public Library Service); transit agencies; the state broadband office; county boards of elections and registration.
dims.programs: State library funding, transit funding, broadband expansion grants, park and recreation programs.

childcare_programs_per1k.label: Licensed child care programs per 1,000 children under 5
childcare_programs_per1k.source: Georgia Department of Early Care and Learning, provider data export; ACS 2020-2024 (children under 5)
childcare_programs_per1k.note: Licensed child care learning centers and family child care learning homes in the state's list on the export date, placed by their address, per 1,000 children under 5. School-age-only programs are left out. A program counts once no matter its size, so this is not a count of slots. Not shown for tracts: families often use care outside their own tract. A tract split by a district line counts its programs by the share of its 2020 residents in each district. 271 of 3825 programs could not be placed at their address. They count in their county and state figures but not in district or tract figures.

childcare_rated_share.label: Licensed programs rated 2 or 3 stars
childcare_rated_share.source: Georgia Department of Early Care and Learning, provider data export (Quality Rated)
childcare_rated_share.note: Share of licensed child care learning centers and family child care learning homes rated 2 or 3 stars in Quality Rated, Georgia's rating system (1 to 3 stars). Programs with no rating count as not rated 2 or 3 stars. A program counts once no matter its size. Not shown for tracts, for the same reason as programs per 1,000 children.

preschool_enrolled.label: Children 3 and 4 enrolled in school or preschool
preschool_enrolled.note: Children ages 3 and 4 enrolled in public or private nursery school, preschool or kindergarten (B14003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
preschool_enrolled.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

grade3_ela_proficient.label: Third graders proficient or above in English language arts (state test)
grade3_ela_proficient.source: Georgia Governor's Office of Student Achievement (GOSA), Georgia Milestones End-of-Grade results; NCES Common Core of Data for school system counties
grade3_ela_proficient.note: Share of tested third graders who scored Proficient or Distinguished on the Georgia Milestones English language arts test. County figures combine the county school system, any city school systems in the county and in-person state charter schools, weighted by the number of students tested; virtual state charter schools and systems too small for GOSA to report are left out. Fewer students tested in 2020-2021. The Georgia figure is built the same way from the same systems so counties compare on equal terms; GOSA's own statewide figure, which counts every school, was 35.1% in 2024-2025. In 2024-2025, 7 counties tested fewer than 30 third graders, so their figures can swing a lot from year to year.

grade3_math_proficient.label: Third graders proficient in math (proficient or above on the state math test)
grade3_math_proficient.source: Georgia Governor's Office of Student Achievement (GOSA), Georgia Milestones End-of-Grade results; NCES Common Core of Data for school system counties
grade3_math_proficient.note: Share of tested third graders who scored Proficient or Distinguished on the Georgia Milestones math test. County figures combine the county school system, any city school systems in the county and in-person state charter schools, weighted by the number of students tested; virtual state charter schools and systems too small for GOSA to report are left out. Fewer students tested in 2020-2021. The Georgia figure is built the same way from the same systems so counties compare on equal terms; GOSA's own statewide figure, which counts every school, was 44.3% in 2024-2025. In 2024-2025, 7 counties tested fewer than 30 third graders, so their figures can swing a lot from year to year. Georgia began testing new math standards in 2023-2024, so earlier years may not compare.

chronic_absent_rate.label: Students chronically absent (missed 10% or more of school)
chronic_absent_rate.source: Georgia Governor's Office of Student Achievement (GOSA), attendance files; NCES Common Core of Data for school system counties
chronic_absent_rate.note: Share of students absent more than 10% of the days they were enrolled, for any reason, excused or not. County figures cover county and city school systems only, weighted by GOSA's student count; state charter schools are left out. The Georgia figure is built the same way from all county and city systems; GOSA's own statewide figure, which counts every school, was 20.4% in 2024-2025. 2019-2020 is left out because school buildings closed in March 2020.

hs_or_higher.label: Adults with a high school diploma or more
hs_or_higher.note: Adults 25 and older with a high school diploma, GED or higher (B15003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
hs_or_higher.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

bachelors_or_higher.label: Adults with a bachelor's degree or more
bachelors_or_higher.note: Adults 25 and older whose highest degree is a bachelor's or higher (B15003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
bachelors_or_higher.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

below_200_share.label: People below 200% of the poverty line
below_200_share.note: People in poverty plus those just above it (C17002). For two adults and two children in 2024, 200% of the Census Bureau's poverty threshold was about $63,600 a year. ± is the 90% margin of error.
below_200_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

poverty_rate.label: People in poverty
poverty_rate.note: People whose family income is below the federal poverty line (C17002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
poverty_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

saipe_child_poverty_rate.label: Child poverty rate, ages 0 to 17 (annual)
saipe_child_poverty_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (SAIPE)
saipe_child_poverty_rate.note: Share of children under 18 below the federal poverty line. SAIPE is a model-based estimate that combines survey, tax and SNAP records, so it gives one value per year; the margin shown is the 90% margin of error.

median_household_income.label: Median household income
median_household_income.note: Half of households earn more and half earn less (B19013). The latest value is in 2024 dollars; earlier periods on the trend line are in their own years' dollars, not adjusted for inflation. District figures are estimated from income brackets (B19001), with no margin of error. ± is the 90% margin of error.
median_household_income.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

places_food_insecurity.label: Adults with food insecurity in the past year
places_food_insecurity.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_food_insecurity.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

gini.label: Income inequality (Gini index)
gini.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates
gini.note: Household income inequality on a scale from 0 (all equal) to 1 (one household has all income) (B19083).

snap_households_share.label: Households that got SNAP food aid (survey)
snap_households_share.note: Households that received SNAP at any time in the past 12 months, as reported in the survey (B22003). Surveys tend to undercount program use. ± is the 90% margin of error.
snap_households_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

snap_persons_share.label: People getting SNAP food aid
snap_persons_share.source: USDA Food and Nutrition Service, SNAP Data Tables (county participation, form FNS-388A); Census Bureau population estimates
snap_persons_share.note: People in households that got SNAP benefits in July, from program records, divided by the Census July 1 population of the same year. The figures stop at July 2023: FNS's county file has no Georgia rows for July 2024 and the July 2025 county lines add up to 28% more than FNS's Georgia total for that month.

unemployment_rate.label: Unemployment rate
unemployment_rate.note: Share of the labor force without a job and looking for one. People are counted where they live, not where they work. County figures come from a BLS model, not a direct count.

prime_age_epop.label: Prime-age workers: share of people 25 to 54 with a job
prime_age_epop.note: People 25 to 54 who are employed (civilian jobs plus armed forces) as a share of all people 25 to 54 (B23001). Places with a prison, college dorms or a nursing home may show a lower rate, since most of those residents are not in the labor force. ± is the 90% margin of error.
prime_age_epop.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

avg_weekly_wage.label: Average weekly wage
avg_weekly_wage.source: BLS Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages
avg_weekly_wage.note: Average weekly pay per job, all employers including government. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation. Jobs are counted where the job is, not where the worker lives. Covers jobs under state unemployment insurance and, in the all-ownership total, federal civilian jobs.

labor_force_change_pct.label: Change in labor force since 2019
labor_force_change_pct.note: Percent change in the labor force from the 2019 annual average. Each series point is that year's change from 2019. People are counted where they live, not where they work. County figures come from a BLS model, not a direct count.

mean_commute.label: Average commute to work
mean_commute.note: Average one-way travel time to work for workers 16 and older who do not work at home (B08013 divided by B08303). ± is the 90% margin of error.
mean_commute.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

rent_burden.label: Renters paying 30% or more of income on rent
rent_burden.note: Renter households whose gross rent is 30% or more of household income (B25070). HUD calls these households cost-burdened. ± is the 90% margin of error.
rent_burden.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

owner_cost_burden.label: Owners with a mortgage paying 30% or more on housing
owner_cost_burden.note: Owner households with a mortgage whose monthly costs are 30% or more of household income (B25091). ± is the 90% margin of error.
owner_cost_burden.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

places_housing_insecurity.label: Adults with housing insecurity in the past year
places_housing_insecurity.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_housing_insecurity.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_utility_shutoff.label: Adults threatened with a utility shutoff in the past year
places_utility_shutoff.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_utility_shutoff.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

overcrowded_share.label: Homes with more than one person per room
overcrowded_share.note: Occupied homes with more than 1.0 occupant per room, owners and renters (B25014). HUD and the Census Bureau use this as a common crowding measure. ± is the 90% margin of error.
overcrowded_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

homeownership.label: Homes lived in by their owners
homeownership.note: Occupied homes that are owner-occupied (B25003). ± is the 90% margin of error.
homeownership.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

vacancy_rate.label: Vacant homes
vacancy_rate.note: Housing units with no one living in them when surveyed, including homes for sale or rent, seasonal homes and abandoned homes (B25002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
vacancy_rate.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

old_housing_share.label: Homes built before 1950
old_housing_share.note: Housing units built in 1949 or earlier (B25034). Age alone does not show a home's condition. ± is the 90% margin of error.
old_housing_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

hud_households_per_1000.label: Households in HUD-subsidized housing, per 1,000 households
hud_households_per_1000.source: HUD Picture of Subsidized Households; Census Bureau American Community Survey and population estimates
hud_households_per_1000.note: Occupied homes in all HUD rental programs (public housing, Housing Choice Vouchers, project-based Section 8, Section 202 and 811 and smaller programs) on Dec. 31, per 1,000 households in the latest ACS 5-year data. Before 2025 HUD published a rounded occupancy rate, not a count, so earlier years are estimates. It counts help received, not results.

places_ghlth.label: Adults in fair or poor health
places_ghlth.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_ghlth.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_diabetes.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_diabetes.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_obesity.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. places_obesity.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_smoking.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_smoking.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

standard.note: The target is age-adjusted and comes from a national survey; the local figures here are not age-adjusted.

uninsured_u65.label: People under 65 without health insurance
uninsured_u65.note: Civilians under 65 not living in institutions who had no health insurance when surveyed (B27010). ± is the 90% margin of error.
uninsured_u65.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

standard.src: Healthy People 2030 national target (AHS-01: 92.4% of people under 65 insured)
standard.note: The target comes from a different national survey (NHIS).

places_checkup.label: Adults with a routine checkup in the past year
places_checkup.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.

places_dental.label: Adults who saw a dentist in the past year
places_dental.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_dental.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

pcp_per100k.label: Primary care doctors per 100,000 people
pcp_per100k.source: HRSA Area Health Resources Files (American Medical Association Physician Masterfile), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
pcp_per100k.note: Practicing non-federal doctors (M.D. and D.O.) under age 75 in general practice, family medicine, general internal medicine and general pediatrics, per 100,000 residents. Counted where the doctor practices, so people may get care in a nearby county.

dentists_per100k.label: Dentists per 100,000 people
dentists_per100k.source: HRSA Area Health Resources Files (CMS National Provider Identifier file), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
dentists_per100k.note: Dentists with a National Provider Identifier, per 100,000 residents. Some may no longer practice or take new patients.

places_mental_distress.label: Adults with frequent mental distress
places_mental_distress.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_mental_distress.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_depression.label: Adults ever told they have depression
places_depression.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_depression.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

overdose_rate_per100k.label: Drug overdose deaths per 100,000 people, past 12 months
overdose_rate_per100k.source: CDC NCHS, VSRR Provisional County-Level Drug Overdose Death Counts; Census Bureau population estimates
overdose_rate_per100k.note: Our calculation: provisional 12-month deaths divided by the Census July 1 population for the year the period ends (2025 population for 2026 periods), times 100,000. Not age-adjusted; blank where CDC hides counts of 1 to 9.

standard.note: The target is age-adjusted; the local rates here are not.

suicide_rate.label: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people (age-adjusted)
suicide_rate.source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics mortality files, via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
suicide_rate.note: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people, age-adjusted, five years combined, by the county where the person lived. Left blank when there were fewer than 20 deaths in the five years.

mh_providers_per100k.label: Mental health providers per 100,000 people
mh_providers_per100k.source: CMS National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPI file), via County Health Rankings & Roadmaps
mh_providers_per100k.note: Psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, counselors, marriage and family therapists, addiction counselors and mental health nurse practitioners with an NPI, per 100,000 residents. Some may no longer practice or take new patients.

violent_crime_rate.label: Violent crime rate
violent_crime_rate.source: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Return A master files
violent_crime_rate.note: Murder, rape, robbery and aggravated assault reported to police, per 100,000 people. Aggravated assault excludes simple assault. Counts only agencies that reported all 12 months, and divides by the population those agencies serve, not the full county. Left blank when those agencies cover less than 80% of the county's people. Crimes reported by campus, park, transit and drug task force police count in their county but add no residents, which raises those counties' rates. An agency that serves more than one county is split by population. The FBI updates its counts after the file used here, so newer FBI totals can differ. Georgia's figure is built the same way, from every Georgia agency that reported all 12 months (299.2 in 2025). The FBI's own statewide estimate, which also estimates crimes for agencies that did not report, is 296.9.

property_crime_rate.label: Property crime rate
property_crime_rate.source: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting Program, Return A master files
property_crime_rate.note: Burglary, larceny-theft and motor vehicle theft reported to police, per 100,000 people. Counts only agencies that reported all 12 months, and divides by the population those agencies serve, not the full county. Left blank when those agencies cover less than 80% of the county's people. Crimes reported by campus, park, transit and drug task force police count in their county but add no residents, which raises those counties' rates. An agency that serves more than one county is split by population. The FBI updates its counts after the file used here, so newer FBI totals can differ. Georgia's figure is built the same way, from every Georgia agency that reported all 12 months (1,404.4 in 2025). The FBI's own statewide estimate, which also estimates crimes for agencies that did not report, is 1,409.3.

traffic_deaths_per100k.label: Traffic deaths per 100,000 people
traffic_deaths_per100k.source: NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS); Census Bureau population estimates
traffic_deaths_per100k.note: Deaths in motor vehicle crashes on public roads, counted in the county where the crash happened, per 100,000 residents per year, five years combined. Not age-adjusted. Left blank when there were fewer than 20 deaths in the five years.

standard.note: The target is age-adjusted and counts deaths where the person lived; the local rates here are not age-adjusted and count deaths where the crash happened.

places_loneliness.label: Adults who feel lonely always, usually or sometimes
places_loneliness.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_loneliness.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

places_emotional_support.label: Adults who lack social and emotional support
places_emotional_support.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_emotional_support.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

voter_turnout.label: Voter turnout, 2024 presidential election
voter_turnout.source: Georgia Secretary of State official results, as compiled by the MIT Election Data + Science Lab; Census Bureau American Community Survey
voter_turnout.note: Votes cast for president divided by U.S. citizens age 18 and older. Ballots left blank for president are not counted. The citizen count is a survey estimate, and it includes some people who cannot vote, such as people serving a felony prison term.

broadband_share.label: Households with a broadband internet subscription
broadband_share.note: Households with a broadband subscription of any type, including a cellular data plan (B28002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
broadband_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

places_no_transportation.label: Adults without reliable transportation in the past year
places_no_transportation.note: CDC model estimate for adults 18 and older (crude prevalence), from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and Census data. It is not a direct count, nearby places can look alike because the model shares information across areas, and CDC says estimates from different PLACES releases should not be compared over time. ± is half the width of CDC's 95% interval. Georgia is the tract values weighted by adults.
places_no_transportation.source: CDC PLACES: Local Data for Better Health, 2025 release

no_vehicle_share.label: Households without a vehicle
no_vehicle_share.note: Occupied homes with no car, van or truck available (B25044). ± is the 90% margin of error.
no_vehicle_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

library_visits_per_capita.label: Public library visits per person
library_visits_per_capita.source: Institute of Museum and Library Services, Public Libraries Survey; Census Bureau population estimates
library_visits_per_capita.note: In-person visits to public libraries in a year, per resident. Some libraries count every visit; others estimate from a typical week. 33 of 60 Georgia library systems have a central or branch library in more than one county. Each such system's total is split among those counties by population, so they share its per-person figure; other systems count in their own county. The Georgia figure adds up all Georgia systems.

social_associations_per10k.label: Membership groups per 10,000 people
social_associations_per10k.source: Census Bureau County Business Patterns; Census Bureau population estimates (definition from County Health Rankings & Roadmaps)
social_associations_per10k.note: Places of worship, civic and social clubs, unions, business and professional groups, political groups, sports clubs, golf and country clubs, fitness centers and bowling alleys with paid staff, per 10,000 residents. Census leaves out any industry with fewer than 3 such places in a county, so small counties are undercounted a little. Georgia's figure is the sum of the county counts, built the same way as the counties; Census's statewide count, which includes the places withheld in county cells, gives 8.7.

bea_snap_per_resident.label: SNAP food benefits per resident
bea_snap_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_snap_per_resident.note: SNAP benefits paid to residents (BEA line 2330), divided by population. BEA starts from USDA's state total and splits it among counties using state payment records, or Census estimates of SNAP recipients where those records are missing. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

bea_ssi_per_resident.label: Supplemental Security Income per resident
bea_ssi_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_ssi_per_resident.note: Federal and state SSI payments to residents who are 65 or older, blind or disabled and have low incomes (BEA line 2310), divided by population. County figures come from Social Security payment data. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

bea_eitc_per_resident.label: Earned income tax credit per resident
bea_eitc_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_eitc_per_resident.note: The federal earned income tax credit for residents (BEA line 2320), divided by population. This is a tax credit: BEA counts the full credit, both the part that lowers taxes owed and the part paid as a refund. County figures come from IRS tax return data. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

bea_veterans_per_resident.label: Veterans' benefits per resident
bea_veterans_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_veterans_per_resident.note: VA pension, disability, education and life insurance benefits and other aid to veterans paid to residents (BEA line 2500), divided by population. County figures come mainly from the VA's report on spending by county. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

bea_unemployment_per_resident.label: Unemployment benefits per resident
bea_unemployment_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_unemployment_per_resident.note: Unemployment insurance paid to residents (BEA line 2400: state programs plus programs for federal workers, railroad workers and former service members), divided by population. Starting with 2022, BEA uses BLS counts of unemployed people to split the state total among counties. 2020 and 2021 include federal pandemic unemployment programs. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

hud_spending_per_resident.label: HUD rental aid spending per resident
hud_spending_per_resident.source: HUD Picture of Subsidized Households; Census Bureau American Community Survey and population estimates
hud_spending_per_resident.note: HUD's average monthly spending per occupied home, times occupied homes, times 12, divided by population. This is a yearly estimate built from a December snapshot, not HUD's reported outlays. Homes HUD could not place in a county are left out of county figures. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

bea_medicaid_per_resident.label: Medicaid and other public medical aid per resident
bea_medicaid_per_resident.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, Regional Accounts table CAINC35; Census Bureau population estimates
bea_medicaid_per_resident.note: Dollars paid for residents' care under Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program and state and local medical aid (BEA line 2220), divided by population. BEA bases county figures on state payment records by county where a state supplies them and spreads the rest using other county data. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

school_spending_per_pupil.label: School spending per pupil (day-to-day costs)
school_spending_per_pupil.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Annual Survey of School System Finances
school_spending_per_pupil.note: Current spending (pay, benefits, supplies, transportation and other day-to-day costs, not buildings or debt) of the traditional school districts based in the county, divided by their fall enrollment. Georgia's figure is built the same way, from all traditional districts. Regional educational service agencies are left out; with them, the Census Bureau's published Georgia figure is $15,833. State charter schools are not in this Census survey. It describes spending, not results. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation.

school_revenue_state_share.label: Share of school district revenue from state sources
school_revenue_state_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Annual Survey of School System Finances
school_revenue_state_share.note: Percent of the revenue of the county's traditional school districts that came from the state of Georgia. Money one school system pays another is left out so it is not counted twice. Georgia's figure is built the same way, from all traditional districts (the Census Bureau's published figure also includes regional educational service agencies: 39.4%). It describes where the money comes from, not results.

library_spend_per_capita.label: Public library spending per person
library_spend_per_capita.source: Institute of Museum and Library Services, Public Libraries Survey; Census Bureau population estimates
library_spend_per_capita.note: Total operating spending by public library systems (staff, materials and other costs; not building projects), in dollars of that year, per resident. 33 of 60 Georgia library systems have a central or branch library in more than one county. Each such system's total is split among those counties by population, so they share its per-person figure; other systems count in their own county. The Georgia figure adds up all Georgia systems.

population.label: Population
population.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

age65_share.label: Residents 65 and older
age65_share.note: Share of all residents who are 65 or older (B01001). ± is the 90% margin of error.
age65_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

prime_age_share.label: Residents ages 25 to 54
prime_age_share.note: Share of all residents who are 25 to 54 (B01001). ± is the 90% margin of error.
prime_age_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_white_share.label: White, not Hispanic
nh_white_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_white_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

nh_black_share.label: Black, not Hispanic
nh_black_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
nh_black_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

hispanic_share.label: Hispanic or Latino (any race)
hispanic_share.note: Share of all residents (B03002). ± is the 90% margin of error.
hispanic_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

foreign_born_share.label: Foreign-born residents
foreign_born_share.note: Residents who were not U.S. citizens at birth, including naturalized citizens (B05012). ± is the 90% margin of error.
foreign_born_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates

disability_share.label: People with a disability
disability_share.note: Civilians not in institutions reporting a hearing, vision, thinking, walking, self-care or independent-living difficulty (B18101). ± is the 90% margin of error.
disability_share.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates
